subject: artificial-intelligence
intro: Artificial intelligence leads to the people who build intelligent systems: researching new methods, turning models into shipped software, mining the data they learn from, and teaching the next cohort.

roles.title: Computer and Information Research Scientists
roles.what: Conduct research into fundamental computer and information science as theorists, designers or inventors, developing solutions to hardware and software problems — including the algorithms behind modern intelligent systems.
roles.where: The search, logical-agent and probabilistic-reasoning units are the classical research canon; the deep learning, reinforcement learning, NLP and computer vision units are the current frontier a research scientist extends.

roles.title: Data Scientists
roles.what: Transform raw data into meaningful information using data-oriented programming languages, applying data mining, data modelling, natural language processing and machine learning to large datasets, then visualising and reporting findings.
roles.where: Learning from examples, learning probabilistic models and deep learning are the training pipeline; the uncertainty and decision-making units supply the principled treatment of noisy data that production machine learning demands.

roles.title: Software Developers
roles.what: Research, design and develop computer and network software or specialised utility programs, analysing user needs and building the software solutions that put AI models into products people actually use.
roles.where: The intelligent agents unit defines the systems developers ship — agents that perceive, decide and act — and the philosophy, ethics and safety of AI unit maps to responsible engineering practice when models go live.

roles.title: Computer Science Teachers, Postsecondary
roles.what: Teach courses in computer science, specialising in fields such as the design and function of computers or operations and research analysis — most combine teaching with their own research.
roles.where: The full course arc — problem-solving by searching, knowledge and reasoning, machine learning, robotics, and philosophy and ethics of AI — is the curriculum a university lecturer in AI delivers and researches.
